model: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, released checkpoint, 48 shards, 510.3 GB, fp8 dense + fp4 experts, no conversion
command: OMP_NUM_THREADS=32 SNAP=/mnt/nvme0/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash [ENV] ./deepseek_v41 8 /tmp/ref.json (25 prompt tokens, 16 generated, cap=8, page cache evicted per run, arms interleaved, 3 runs each)

hardware.cpu: 2x Intel Xeon Platinum 8555C, 52 cores/socket, 2 threads/core = 104 physical cores, 208 logical CPUs, 4 NUMA nodes
hardware.storage: A: Samsung MZQL2960HCJR (nvme0n1, 894 GB) ext4 noatime, /mnt/nvme0. B: 2x Samsung MZQLB7T6HMLA (7.6 TB) in RAID0 (md0) ext4, /mdr5. A and B are independent controllers.

hypothesis: Reading the routed experts with O_DIRECT instead of through the page cache raises the expert read rate and, with the CPU side in order, the decode rate.

quality.method: token-exact vs a 16-token reference stream; the engine exits non-zero on any mismatch. All runs 16/16, in both regimes. tok_s is 16 generated tokens over the whole turn (READY to DONE), prefill included, with the engine's OpenMP team set to 32 threads (OMP_NUM_THREADS=32) so the CPU side is not the bottleneck -- see PR #1517 for why that matters
